narrativeBlocks.title: Medea supplies essential help
narrativeBlocks.body: In Apollonius' Argonautica, Medea gives Jason a protective charm for the dangerous task. The epic connects his success to her knowledge.

narrativeBlocks.title: The charm changes the contest
narrativeBlocks.body: Verbatim from Seaton's translation: “And forth from her fragrant girdle ungrudgingly she brought out the charm; and he at once received it in his hands with joy.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Euripides begins later
narrativeBlocks.body: The Nurse in Medea remembers the Argo's voyage, then says Jason has married Creon's daughter while Medea is dishonored.

narrativeBlocks.title: Do not merge epic and tragedy
narrativeBlocks.body: Apollonius narrates a quest and Medea's aid; Euripides stages the consequences of Jason's later marriage. These works preserve different moments and genres.

narrativeBlocks.title: The same names carry different claims
narrativeBlocks.body: A successful voyage does not settle the obligations that the tragedy brings forward.
